PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation. 

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Councilmember Lainez requested to pull Item 6 from the Consent Agenda.

Assistant City Manager Domic provided a brief overview of Item 6.
Mayor Pro Tem  Lainez noted that while local jurisdictions are generally expected to contribute approximately 3% of the cost, for the City of Commerce, this contribution could range from $7 to $10 million. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez emphasized the importance of exploring other potential investments related to transportation projects.

Assistant City Manager Domic acknowledged that these options had been discussed. However, he explained that certain infrastructure projects, such as a bike lane along Smithway, were not feasible due to traffic constraints and the planned expansion of the Citadel. He further noted that the City had proposed a pedestrian bridge over the I-5 freeway, but the proposal was not approved. Other initiatives under consideration include a walking path from Goodrich to the Mixmaster area and a combined pedestrian and bike path along Telegraph Road.

Councilmember Lainez pointed out that the project does not start until 2029, and the City has time to explore all available opportunities. He also requested that staff review the Transit-Oriented Plan, which is nearing finalization, as it includes infrastructure recommendations that could contribute to the required 3% investment.

City Manager Hernandez noted that other cities in the region share similar concerns and that in-kind contributions, as well as certain transportation department expenditures, could be counted toward the required contribution. The City has maintained that the 3% contributions come from immediately impacted cities, as the entire region stands to benefit from the project. However, there are multiple ways to meet this requirement.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez inquired whether the current action was solely to enter into an agreement, with negotiations on the 3% contribution to be addressed at a later stage.

Councilmember Lainez moved to approve Eastside Transit Corridor Phase 2 Project Cooperative Agreement with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority, and Councilmember Argumedo seconded the motion. The item passed unanimously with a 5-0-0 vote.

Mayor Altamirano closed public hearing.  
Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway provided a brief overview of the staff report.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo expressed gratitude to the Parks and Recreation Department for organizing the Snow Day event and congratulated the Downey High School women's water polo team, which includes many players from Commerce. She also thanked the Library Department for hosting the African Drum Circle, noting that it was a wonderful event.


Councilmember Argumedo extended his appreciation to everyone who contributed to the success of the Snow Day event. He reported attending the ICA Conference in Santa Barbara, where he participated in sessions on functional zero homelessness and new policing technologies. Additionally, he met with Sergeant Jimenez to discuss current community issues.


Councilmember Garcia also attended the ICA Conference in Santa Barbara, where her sessions focused on economic development and advancements in police technologies.


Mayor Pro Tem Lainez thanked the City departments involved in the Snow Day event and took a moment to wish his son a happy birthday, celebrating his milestone of becoming a teenager.


Mayor Altamirano reported that he also attended the ICA Conference.



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 6:48 p.m. in memory of Minerva Morales.
